chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant may make a condition (exception) for himself for a period of up to forty days if he forgets (to specify a time).'

key_terms.يَسْتَثْنِيَ: To make a condition or exception (in the context of a vow)

ai.seo_question: What is the default duration for a vow if no time is specified or forgotten?
ai.summary: In the context of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the default duration for indefinite vows (al-ayman al-muṭlaqa) when the vow-maker forgets the term, establishing a forty-day period as the standard limit for fulfillment. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for resolving ambiguity in personal vows, ensuring that obligations are not left open-ended indefinitely. It reflects the practical legal principle of providing a reasonable timeframe for compliance when specific conditions are omitted or forgotten.
